purpose: Teach: 部首/肉食/賢者/胃腸/貧富/剰余/分娩/既知

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、漢字の部首分類の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper was on kanji radical classification, wasn't it?
lines.style: Steady, genuine interest. Light emphasis on 「蓮さん」 — checking in with him. Warm but professional. The tone of someone who's read the work and wants to hear him talk about it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、肉食動物の生態学を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I wrote on the ecology of carnivores.
lines.style: Respectful, slightly careful. Crisp delivery without rushing. A small pause before the answer, like he's making sure he understood the question correctly.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、古代インドの賢者像を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I thought your paper focused on sage figures in ancient India?
lines.style: Gentle pause. Thoughtful tone — not accusatory, more like she's working through something with him. Slightly softer on the question mark, inviting clarification rather than pointing out confusion.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、ストレス性胃腸障害の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — my research was on stress-related gastric disorders.
lines.style: Straightforward, patient. No defensiveness. The tone of someone stating fact while remaining open to wherever this conversation is going. Slight lift at the start, grounding at the end.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 社会の貧富の差を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You explored wealth inequality in society through your thesis, didn't you?
lines.style: Present and engaged. Clear articulation. A half-beat of warmth beneath the question — she's genuinely interested in the topic. Light on the question tag, inviting rather than testing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、整数論の剰余類の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on modular arithmetic and residue classes in number theory.
lines.style: Measured, precise. Each phrase deliberate. The delivery of someone who knows his material deeply and is explaining it clearly. No hesitation, but not rushed either.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、無痛分娩の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper examined the history of painless childbirth, correct?
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly searching. Lower register on the opening — like she's testing a hypothesis with him gently. Reflective pause before the final word, respectful of the topic's weight.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、既知のデータと新発見の比較を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I compared established data with new findings from my research.
lines.style: Calm, concise. A touch of quiet confidence. The close carries a subtle sense of completion — he's answered clearly and he's waiting to see where she's heading with this line of questioning.
